title: Lonesome Crow
scene: Hanover early hard rock / psychedelic-prog and Krautrock crossover
notes: Exploratory dark psych-rock, jointly tracked in studio, with Michael Schenker and extended improvisations.

title: Fly to the Rainbow
scene: West German hard rock / progressive-psychedelic transition
notes: Roth joins; acoustic passages, Hendrix-inspired guitar, expansive structures and a harder riffing attack.

title: In Trance
scene: German melodic hard rock / early heavy metal
notes: Dierks tightens the songwriting into brisk metal riffs, bittersweet ballads and expressive guitar solos.

title: Virgin Killer
scene: German hard rock / emerging European heavy metal
notes: Compact, urgent guitar rock preserves Roth’s winding psychedelic leads and reflective slower songs.

title: Taken by Force
scene: Hanover hard rock / early European heavy metal
notes: Uli Jon Roth’s final studio album; elaborate guitar passages meet forceful hard-rock songs.

title: Lovedrive
scene: West German melodic hard rock and arena rock
notes: Jabs and Michael Schenker share guitar duties; sharper hooks, acoustic ballads, a reggae diversion.

title: Animal Magnetism
scene: German hard rock / melodic heavy metal
notes: Dark grooves, The Zoo’s talk box, and unusual orchestration beside the guitar-heavy core.

title: Blackout
scene: German arena hard rock / 1980s heavy metal
notes: Concentrated riffs and melodic choruses mark Meine’s vocal comeback after surgery.

title: Love at First Sting
scene: West German arena hard rock and melodic heavy metal
notes: Digitally recorded guitar anthems, stadium hooks, and the slow-burning ballad Still Loving You.

title: Savage Amusement
scene: German late-1980s polished melodic hard rock
notes: Glossy pop-metal edges and lush melodies soften riffs; Believe in Love closes on longing.

title: Crazy World
scene: German melodic hard rock with early-1990s power ballads
notes: Heavier melodic rock meets the peace anthem Wind of Change and acoustic power ballads.

title: Face the Heat
scene: Early-1990s German hard rock / heavy metal
notes: Heavier riffs and social commentary meet acoustic passages and unusual sitar and E-Bow touches.
